subject: POC scope: token economics, latency SLOs, and deployment options
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC scope: token economics, latency SLOs, and deployment options

Hi Megan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap of your requirements
- Target workloads: patient triage chat + batch summarization of visit notes.
- Approx current traffic: 60k MAU (mostly triage) with peak concurrency in mornings.
- Average prompt+response tokens (estimate): 300 tokens for triage, 6k tokens for nightly summarization jobs.
- Latency SLO for triage: p90 < 300ms for UI responses (mobile web). Summaries can be batch and tolerate higher latency.

2) Pricing / volume guidance we discussed
- You said the target unit economics goal is roughly $400–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on mode (streaming vs batched) and SLA.
- Shortlist: hosted API for initial POC; Dedicated (reserved) if predictable throughput and tighter p95 targets required.

3) Suggested POC plan (low lift)
- 2-week seeded POC: hosted endpoints + token usage tracking, plus one small dedicated node for a canary to validate p90 under load.
- We'll run an ingestion job to emulate nightly summarization and real-time triage traffic.
- Deliverables: token burn report, latency percentiles, cost/1M breakdown, concrete tuning recommendations (batch size, streaming vs chunking).

Attachments: I attached a preliminary pricing sheet (redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx) with example unit economics for the traffic profile you shared.

Next steps: can you confirm the ballpark monthly token burn we should model (pick one): A) 200M, B) 500M, or C) 1B? Also confirm if EHR PHI constraints require a Private deployment for the POC.

If that looks right, I’ll set up an engineering sync (30–45m) for next week and spin up the initial telemetry.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC scope: token economics, latency SLOs, and deployment options

Thanks Neha — this is super helpful. A few clarifications: 

- Ballpark monthly tokens: we'd model B) ~500M tokens to start (triage dominates). Nightly summaries add variability; expect 2x spike over 3–4 nights per month.
- PHI: yes, everything is within our VPC today; for the POC we need to verify encryption and SOC2 artifacts. Private deployment preferred if it's low overhead, but we can start hosted if you can guarantee encryption in transit/storage and a SOC2 attestation.
- Latency: p90 < 300ms is critical for the triage UI. If that pushes pricing up, we can consider a hybrid: streaming for triage (lower latency, higher cost) + batched summarization on cheaper nodes.

Megan
Megan Liu
Platform PM, Acme Health

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC scope: token economics, latency SLOs, and deployment options

Hi Megan — noted on 500M tokens and PHI requirements. Short reply with concrete economics and the trade-offs so you have something to share with procurement: 

A) Hosted vs Dedicated unit economics (very high level)- Hosted (shared): lower up-front but higher per-1M token cost; good for quick POC. Example: $1,200 / 1M tokens under p90 < 300ms streaming configuration (includes streaming premium).
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): $600–$850 / 1M tokens if you commit a monthly baseline (savings from utilization, quantization options). Better when you hit sustained volume > ~400M tokens/month.

B) Streaming vs Batch- Streaming (real-time token-by-token, lower latency): higher cost, best for triage UI and p90 targets. Also minimizes user-perceived latency.
- Batching (batch inference + async response): much cheaper for long summarization jobs — can be 3–6x lower $/1M depending on batch sizes and KV cache reuse.

C) SLO-driven tiering we recommend for cost control- Tier 1: triage traffic routed to streaming-hosted or a small dedicated pool (p90 < 300ms)- Tier 2: async summarization to batching nodes with larger sequence optimizations- Use smart routing so only the latency-critical fraction hits the higher-cost path. This preserves overall $/1M.

D) Next steps and asks for the engineering sync- Confirm whether Acme can provide a short anonymized sample of triage traffic (300 tokens typical) and a sample of a 6k-token note for tuning.- Are there any internal constraints on outbound cloud endpoints to spin up a hosted canary? If no, we’ll provision a hosted canary; if yes, we’ll scope Private trial.

I’ll attach a short example of the token burn table and two scenario runs in the XLSX. If we agree on POC scope, I recommend a 2-week POC starting the week of Mar 21 to capture daily patterns.

Best,
Neha

Subject: Acme Health (RDW-4581) — recommended POC and credit ask (internal)

Internal only — looping you in after the external thread. Key points: Acme expects ~500M/mo and requires PHI handling. They prefer a Private option but are open to hosted if SOC2 artifacts and encryption are available. P90 <300ms for triage is must-have.

Recommendation: offer 2-week hosted POC with a 1-node dedicated canary and 10k free tokens/day credit + engineering support. This keeps friction low while we validate latency at scale. If PHI prevents hosted endpoints, propose Private trial with on-prem connector (longer lead).

Action items:
- Rishi: can you validate the dedicated canary spec (GPU type & expected p90) and cost delta?
- Priyom: prepare a short SOC2 & encryption summary to send to Acme.
- Evelyn: CS backup for onboarding/telemetry.

If everyone agrees, I’ll send the external proposal and attach the XLSX pricing.

Neha
